qt: to the Commission Lina Gálvez (S&D), Mohammed Chahim (S&D), Leire Pajín (S&D) Subject:

On 9 July 2026, the forest fire in Los Gallardos-Bédar (Almería) killed 15 people; 14 of the victims were not Spanish, and nationals of other Member States were among those who died. No ES-Alert messages were sent to the public’s mobile phones. The Andalusian Parliament refused to set up a committee of inquiry and, as a result, families fear that only criminal liability will be established. Article 110 of Directive (EU) 2018/1972 regulates public alerts over mobile networks; Decision No 1313/2013/EU provides for risk prevention and planning, including early warnings; and the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union protects the right to life (Article 2) and the right to an effective remedy (Article 47). In light of the above: 1.

Has the Commission requested information from the Spanish authorities as to why the alert was not triggered and assessed compliance with Article 110 of Directive (EU) 2018/1972 and the prevention plans in accordance with the EU Civil Protection Mechanism?
Does it consider the absence of a public, independent investigation – in parallel with the criminal investigation – to be in line with Articles 2 and 47 of the Charter?
What measures will it take to ensure that public warning systems are used effectively in the event of forest fires, while respecting the cultural diversity of the population?
